sections.title: Visiting and gathering
sections.content: *meglátogat* ("to visit") and *összejön* ("to get together") are the two verbs that make family life sentences work. Both conjugate the way you already know: *meglátogatom*, *meglátogatod*... *összejövök*, *összejössz*...

sections.title: The object ending after a possessive
sections.content: When a possessed noun is the object, the accusative *-t* goes after the possessive ending. After *-m* or *-d* a linking vowel comes first: *szüleimet*, *szüleidet*, *anyámat*, *testvéremet*. After the plain *-i* of *szülei* it is just *-t*: *szüleit*. A possessed object is specific, so the verb is definite: *meglátogatom*, not *meglátogatok*.

items.english: On Sunday I'm visiting Károly's parents.

sections.content: *meglátogatom* uses the definite conjugation you already know from A1 — *meglátogatom Károly szüleit* has a specific, known object (Károly's parents), so it takes *-om*, not *-ok*.
